analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md it adds one row at head line 1960 to the LaunchAgent passthrough variable table for DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS. In docs/reference/configuration.md line 685 it changes "Not forwarded to LaunchAgents" to "Forwarded to the launchd provider job". No executable code is in the supplied diff, so I could not verify that the source actually forwards the variable (LaunchAgent.swift passthroughEnvKeys/inferencePassthroughEnvKeys).

Threat relevance is T-041 (prefix-cache at-rest tier). The variable is a tighten-or-loosen performance knob: a negative value writes complete checkpoints instead of deltas. It does not change the T-041 controls that are the sign-off focus: HMAC lookup names, AAD construction, the 30-minute TTL, disk budget, KEK wipe, authenticated salt scoping and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. Forwarding a shell value into the plist only extends an already default-on, locally operator-controlled setting to the daemon, so it creates no new trust boundary. The operator is the local user who already controls the plist. Incremental versus complete checkpoint writes use the same DBK3 encryption, so I found no at-rest exposure change.

Cross-file consistency: the two docs now agree with each other. One residual inconsistency is that configuration.md line 683 (MAX_STAGE_MB/MS) still says it is not forwarded. That is consistent with the cli-reference table, which does not list it, but the SSD write-budget and disk variables at cli-reference lines 1936-1943 are described separately and stay consistent. The next pass should confirm that the source passthrough list includes this key. If the key is not actually forwarded, the docs would be inaccurate, which is a documentation drift issue and not a security regression.

No findings. needs_deeper_review is false because the change is documentation-only and low risk. The only unverified contract is the passthrough code, which is outside the supplied evidence.
